purpose: explain the 32-caller tail latency, measure the ready queue against the channel handoffs it replaced, and compare engines
before_after_runs: 20 rounds, alternating which tree runs first; each round runs BenchmarkLatency go-worker (100000x), then BenchmarkPool and BenchmarkConcurrentSubmit go-worker with default benchtime, -count=1
engine_runs: 20 rounds on the after tree, rotating the engine order; each engine runs BenchmarkPool, BenchmarkConcurrentSubmit, and BenchmarkLatency with default benchtime, -count=1
traces: 3 runs per tree of BenchmarkLatency/Noop/workers=8/callers=32/go-worker with -test.trace, analyzed with golang.org/x/exp/trace; traces and analysis programs are not kept in the repository
diagnostics: GOGC=off, -cpu=16, Submit instead of Schedule, and runtime.Gosched after each reply were run on the before tree or patched copies of it; only summaries are recorded
